items.front: The four language families of India (and the two largest shares)?
Earliest Indian script and its direction; the Gandhara script?
items.back: Brahmi (left-to-right), parent of most Indian scripts; Kharosthi was written right-to-left.

items.front: First classical language of India, and the year Telugu got the tag?
Oldest Tamil grammar and the twin Sangam epics?
items.back: Tolkappiyam; epics Silappadikaram (Ilango Adigal) and Manimekalai (Sathanar).

items.front: The Telugu Kavitrayam and their joint work?
items.back: Nannaya ('Adi Kavi'), Tikkana and Yerrapragada (Errana) — the Andhra Mahabharatam.

items.front: Author-king of Amuktamalyada and patron of the Ashtadiggajas?
items.back: Krishnadevaraya (Vijayanagara); his eight court poets were the Ashtadiggajas.

items.front: Leader of the Ashtadiggajas, 'Andhra Kavita Pitamaha'; his work?
Two celebrated non-court Telugu poets — a Bhagavatam and a Ramayana?
items.back: Bammera Pothana (Andhra Maha Bhagavatam) and Atukuri Molla (a Telugu Ramayana); Vemana wrote moral Satakam verse.

items.front: The six orthodox (Astika) schools of Indian philosophy?
items.back: Samkhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mimamsa, Vedanta (Samkhya, by Kapila, is oldest).

items.front: How many dances does the Sangeet Natak Akademi call 'classical'?
items.back: Eight; the Ministry of Culture adds Chhau (nine). All rest on Bharata's Natya Shastra.

items.front: AP's classical dance, its codifier and signature item?
items.back: Kuchipudi; codified by Siddhendra Yogi (Bhamakalapam); signature Tarangam (plate dance).
Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Shyama Shastri; M.S. Subbulakshmi was first musician with a Bharat Ratna.
items.examPoint: Indian classical music — Carnatic vs Hindustani

items.back: Decimal place-value, use of zero, value of π, and eclipses explained by the earth's rotation (Aryabhatiya, 5th c.).

items.front: Match: Varahamihira, Brahmagupta, Sushruta, Charaka — to their fields.
items.back: Varahamihira: Brihat Samhita (astronomy); Brahmagupta: zero/negatives; Sushruta: surgery; Charaka: medicine/Ayurveda.
